newsitem.title: INDIA: India plans third asset sale in February 1997.
newsitem.headline: India plans third asset sale in February 1997.

text.p: India is planning to make a third round of asset sale in February, 1997 through a partial sell-off of stake in 40 state-owned units, a government official said on Friday.
"We are looking at 40 public sector sector undertakings," G.V. Ramakrishna, head of a special panel in charge of the sale told newspersons.
He said the panel would analyse the financial viability, profitability and evaluate shares in the state-owned units to see if divestment would fetch fair prices for them.
India plans to raise 50 billion rupees from divestment of shares in state-owned units in 1996/97 (April-March).
"Total government investment in equity and loans is about 1,720 billion rupees in 245 enterprises," Ramakrishna said.
The government had already announced partial sale of shares in Indian Oil Corporation and Videsh Sanchar Nigam Limited in the first round of disinvestment.
The exact dates of the first round of divestment has not been announced. A second round is expected to follow soon after OIL and VSNL.
The panel, known as the Disinvestment Commission, will not be in charge of the first two rounds.
"We (the panel) are expected to come in around from the third tranch. The third tranche of disinvestment will be around February," Ramakrishna said.

The panel held discussions early this week with merchant bankers, financial institutions, domestic as well as foreign, credit rating agencies and academics to discuss ways to get a fair value of shares.
"The shares will be offered locally as well as in the international markets," he said.

Ramakrishna said Oil and Natural Gas Corporation, Oil India Limited, Bongaingaon Refineries, Steel Authority of India Limited, Mahanagar Telephone Nigam Limited, Gas Authority of India Limited, Shipping Corporation of India, Engineers India Limited, Indian Tourism Development Corporation, Air India were some of the firms in the list of 40 state-owned units.

The others were Hindustan Aeronautics limited, Air India, Container Corporation of India, Indian Petrochemical Limited, Fertilizer and Chemicals Travancore, National Fertilizers limited, Madras Fertilizers, Hotel Corporation of India, Pawan Hans, Neyveli Lignite Corporation, Hindustan Teleprinter, Northern Coalfields, South-eastern coalfields, Western coalfields, Indian Telephone Industries, Bharat Earth Movers Limited, Bharat Electronics Limited, Modern Food Industry and Hindustan Latex.

Ramakrishna said Bharat Aluminium Company Ltd, Hindustan Copper Limited, Hindustan Zinc Limited, National Aluminium Company Limited, IBP, National Thermal Power Corporation, Power Grid Corporation Ltd, National Hydro Power Corporation, Rail India Technical and Economic Services, Kudremukh Iron Ore Company and Maganese Ore India Limited.
